analysis: The PR changes only documentation: docs/developer/test.md (new "Add-On Hold" test section at head lines 768-790 plus a date bump) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (new `darkbloom addon` command row, section at head ~904-932, and an add-on runtime file row at ~1758). No executable code, no policy, and no threat-model definitions are changed, so no control is weakened by these files. The docs describe a new local control surface that is not in the supplied source: a root-less AF_UNIX socket (`~/.darkbloom/runtime/addon.sock`, 0600), an `addon-hold.json` record, an `ownership.lock` flock, and an owner-only lifecycle mailbox bound to live process identity. A hold closes admission, drains for up to 120 s and unloads all models. `release --force` can release while an add-on holds the machine lock. This is new attack surface (local DoS or availability manipulation of the provider, TB-003 operator/process boundary, plus peer authentication of the add-on and hold lease semantics, T-010/T-029 availability class). The implementation (AddonHoldPaths, ProviderLoop+AddonHold, AddonIPCServer, AddonPeerPolicy) is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot judge its soundness. The docs say the peer-policy is tested only negatively (the test runner has no signed add-on), and the authenticator is stubbed in socket and loop flows; this is a documented coverage limit, not a regression. The docs also say a held provider reports a draining heartbeat and rejects with 503. This is a state-visibility/availability interaction with the coordinator wire contract (TB-002) that code review should confirm does not weaken App Attest authorization (TB-011) or leak plaintext. The threat model may need an entry for the add-on IPC and mailbox boundary once the code lands. Examined docs claims for contradictions with the base threat model (no claims of attestation, secrecy or receipt changes) and found none.
